title: Hosted API escalation debrief and proactive fix pack for 5xx/timeouts during tenant retry storms
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Summary:
During a multi-tenant surge on 2025-02-19 we observed sustained 5xx errors and timeouts in the Hosted API. Multiple high-revenue customers escalated to SEs and SRE; symptoms included long tail latency, request retries amplifying backend load, and socket pool exhaustion on proxy and model-serving tiers. This ticket captures the root cause, the emergency mitigations applied, the permanent fixes landed, and the rollout/verification plan across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private environments.
steps_to_reproduce: Replay tenant-pattern: high-volume small-burst requests (~30RPS/tenant) with synthetic client retry behavior (exponential backoff with capped jitter).
Inject transient 502 from a model-serving node to trigger client/edge retries and measure amplification factor.
Observe kvcache eviction and connection churn in staging with tenant-weighted load generator (tools/loadbench v0.9).
root_cause_summary: A cascade started when a set of model-serving workers briefly exceeded latency SLOs due to a concurrent KV cache compaction schedule. Proxies retried non-idempotent requests aggressively, and our connection admission logic allowed many inflight retries to stack. Two contributing factors: 1) 'retry amplification' from per-tenant client libraries + edge retries, and 2) synchronous KV compaction and eviction causing transient GPU stalls; together these exceeded proxy connection pools and triggered 5xx responses upstream.
mitigation_applied: Deployed proxy-side conservative retry-shedding: cap per-tenant concurrent retries to 4 and short-circuit further retries with 429 + retry-after when quota exhausted.
Fast hotpatch to model-serving: stagger KV compaction windows across az/replica and reduce compaction CPU share to avoid GPU stall overlap.
Enabled temporary tenant-priority fastpath for escalated customers to prevent their requests being dropped while global backpressure ramped.
Adjusted SDK defaults in Hosted for 2s -> 1s backoff floor to reduce synchronized retries (short-term).
Opened customer communications: status page updates + targeted emails to impacted accounts (INC-2025-042).
fix_details: Permanent fixes landed in runtime-1.21: 1) Admission controller change to enforce inflight-retry quotas and differentiate idempotent vs non-idempotent payloads; 2) KV cache compaction refactor to use async compaction with per-replica jitter and a max-CPI budget; 3) Proxy change to honor idempotency-key header and route idempotent-safe hedged requests to read-only fastpath; 4) SDK update 2.3.1 to default to jittered exponential backoff and surface client-side idempotency helper. See PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2314, https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/1460, https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/512
rollout_plan: Canary deploy runtime-1.21 to 3% of hosts in us-west-2 for 2 hours, monitor error-rate and tail-99 latency.
If metrics stable, expand to 25% over next 4 hours, then to 100% in 24 hours with automated watch gates.
Coordinate Dedicated customers: preflight bundle and operator advisory; schedule maintenance windows where requested.
For Private customers: publish advisory plus patch instructions; offer remote assist where customers run pinned older runtimes.
verification_metrics: Hosted API 5xx-rate < 0.02% (measured per-tenant) during peak simulated load
P99 latency for small payloads reduced to baseline +-10%
Inflow retry amplification factor (total requests / unique client intents) < 1.5
Connection pool saturation events down to zero for 30m sustained window
rollback_plan: Rollback route: if any canary experiences >2x baseline 5xx or P99 increases >30% for 15 minutes, automatically rollback via control-plane to previous runtime version. Run emergency mitigation (re-enable hot-shed logic) and open escalation bridge. Documented in runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/hosted/retry-storm-rollback
